messages:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool 'inference-gpu' exhausted in us-west-2. HPA for inference service not scaling (external metrics missing). Queue growth on /v1/generate, spike in 5xx/429s. Paging SRE oncall.
Emma W: on it, thanks. I'm joining. Can someone grab initial customer impact numbers?
Ana S: support FYI — several customers have reported timeouts and 503s; top ticket from acme-corp (prod) reporting repeated 504s since ~11:40 UTC.
Raj P: looking. First suspicion: Prometheus adapter / metrics-server pipeline lag. I see adapter errors in logs.
Raj P: tailing prometheus-adapter:
```
I0315 11:42:10.123 adapter.go:211] Querying external metric 'inference_queue_length'
W0315 11:42:12.456 adapter.go:320] failed to query external metrics: context deadline exceeded
E0315 11:42:12.456 adapter.go:431] returning no metrics for inference_queue_length
```

Raj P: metrics-server also has noisy errors:
```
E0315 11:41:59.789 metrics_server.go:102] failed to get resource metrics: no metrics returned from scraping
E0315 11:42:00.001 status.go:78] failed to list nodes: Get "https://10.0.0.1:443/api/v1/nodes": net/http: TLS handshake timeout
```

Emma W: that matches the HPA behavior—external metrics are missing so HPA stays at min replicas and queue grows. Are we seeing network issues to prometheus?
Raj P: running prometheus query for scrape timestamps: `up{job="node-exporter"}` shows some targets down. Also seeing spikes in prometheus write latency.
Jon Ops: noticed control-plane load on the metrics cluster around that time; possible temporary overload on prometheus or ssd I/O.
Emma W: immediate mitigation options: 1) temporarily override HPA and scale deployment replicas manually to relieve queue, 2) restart prometheus-adapter / metrics-server pods, 3) if needed, scale node pool or enable spare capacity. Thoughts?
Maria G: I'll prepare the canary manual scale. We should prefer restarting adapter first since manual scale is heavier.
Raj P: restarting prometheus-adapter now (kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deployment prometheus-adapter). I'll monitor adapter logs.
Oncall Bot: :white_check_mark: Action logged: prometheus-adapter restart (initiated by Raj P).
Raj P: after restart adapter logs show successful queries but with lag catch-up. HPA still hasn't reconciled because metrics API returned empty for several windows.
Emma W: Maria, please do a manual scale to get urgent traffic through. Use `kubectl scale deployment inference-dep -n inference --replicas=8`. We'll roll back after autoscaling recovers.
Maria G: scaling now.
Maria G: `kubectl scale` returned success, replicas scaling from 2 -> 8. Watching pods come up.
Ana S: started updating affected customers: acme-corp notified of mitigation and ETA ~5-10m.
Jon Ops: also kicked off a node-pool resize as precaution (gke resize to add 4 nodes) to avoid scheduling bottlenecks while pods start.
Raj P: prometheus-adapter logs look normal now, and metrics-server restarted (kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment metrics-server) — metrics are being returned but there is still a backlog.
Raj P: Running `kubectl get hpa -n inference` shows HPA target metric starting to report but still 0/target for a couple cycles.
Emma W: good. keep manual scale until HPA resumes autonomous scaling. Track queue length and tail app logs for throttles.
Raj P: paste from adapter after restart: `INFO: external metrics fetched 150 samples for inference_queue_length; latency=1.2s`
Maria G: pods are Ready, request rate is dropping, 5xxs decreasing. Support says acme-corp saw improvement.
Ana S: confirmed — acme-corp ticket updated: throughput improved, no errors in last 3 minutes.
Jon Ops: node pool scale completed, new nodes Ready. Scheduler backlog cleared.
Emma W: summary for next handoff: cause appears to be Prometheus/adapter latency leading to HPA not receiving external metrics -> HPA stuck at min replicas -> GPU pool exhausted -> queue growth and client-facing errors. Immediate fixes applied: restarted prometheus-adapter and metrics-server, manually scaled deployment to 8 replicas, scaled node pool + monitored recovery.
Emma W: impact: multiple customers experienced elevated latency and some 5xx/504 errors for ~20 minutes, highest impact customers were high-request tenants.
Raj P: next steps (short): 1) investigate root cause of prometheus slowness (storage/backpressure, query timeouts), 2) add more robust alerting for adapter error rate and metrics lag, 3) add HPA fallback to resource-based metrics if external metric missing for >2 windows, 4) create a runbook step to perform safe manual scale and node-pool spin-up.
Maria G: I'm taking the on-call handoff. Capturing timeline and actions in the incident doc. Adding command snippets used to mitigation to the runbook:
```
# manual scale
kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-dep --replicas=8
# restart adapter
kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deployment prometheus-adapter
# restart metrics-server
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment metrics-server
```
Emma W: thanks Maria. I'll open the postmortem and link logs + prometheus snapshots. Also we should check RBAC or TLS issues that led to metrics-server TLS handshake timeouts in logs.
Ana S: support to follow up with affected customers with incident summary and mitigation steps.
Oncall Bot: :spiral_notepad: Incident ticket created INC-2026-0415-17 with priority P1.
Maria G: handing off to operations for deeper root cause. I'll stay on for the next 15m for context if anything flares.
Emma W: appreciated. I'll drop a note in #exec with high-level impact.
Raj P: sampling additional checks: cluster disk I/O had a spike preceding the adapter timeouts; collecting iostat and prometheus WAL metrics for postmortem.
Maria G: final note before shift: HPA resumed and auto-scaled to 6 replicas after external metric catch-up. Manual scale will be rolled down to baseline once we confirm stability.
Ana S: customer notifications queued.
Emma W: closing active mitigation. Documenting action items and assignment for postmortem (Raj for metrics infra, Jon for node pool autoscaler tuning, Maria for runbook updates, Ana for customer comms).
Maria G: :wave: taking over. If anything else shows up ping me directly.
Oncall Bot: :lock: Incident moved to monitoring state. Last update logged.
